title_en: Lu Tingzuo v. Shanghai Zhabei District Housing and Land Administration Bureau — dispute over administrative ruling on house demolition
ruling_gist_en: During the process of house demolition, if the person whose house is being demolished or the house tenant has objections to the appraisal report of the demolished house, they have the right to apply for re-appraisal. Therefore, based on the principle of due process, in order to protect the right of the person whose house is being demolished and the house tenant to apply for re-appraisal of the appraisal report according to law, the demolition party shall timely deliver the appraisal report of the demolished house to the person whose house is being demolished and the house tenant. During the adjudication process, the administrative adjudication authority for house demolition shall also ascertain whether the appraisal report of the demolished house has been delivered to the person whose house is being demolished and the house tenant, and ensure that the appraisal report is delivered to the person whose house is being demolished and the house tenant before the adjudication is made. If the administrative adjudication authority for house demolition issues an administrative adjudication on house demolition without ascertaining this issue, and cannot provide evidence to prove that the appraisal report of the demolished house has been delivered to the person whose house is being demolished and the house tenant, the administrative adjudication on house demolition so made shall be deemed as having unclear findings of fact, insufficient key evidence, and violating statutory procedures. If the person whose house is being demolished or the house tenant brings a lawsuit to the people's court requesting the revocation of such adjudication, the people's court shall grant support.

full_text_en:
Lu Tingzuo v. Shanghai Zhabei District Housing and Land Administration Bureau — dispute over administrative ruling on house demolition

Ruling Summary

During the process of house demolition, if the person whose property is being demolished or the lessee of the house has an objection to the appraisal report of the demolished house, they are entitled to apply for a re-evaluation. Therefore, based on the principle of due process, in order to protect the right of the person whose property is being demolished or the lessee of the house to apply for a re-evaluation of the appraisal report of the demolished house in accordance with the law, the demolishing party shall deliver the appraisal report of the demolished house to the person whose property is being demolished or the lessee of the house in a timely manner. The administrative ruling authority for house demolition, during the ruling process, should also ascertain whether the appraisal report of the demolished house has been delivered to the person whose property is being demolished or the lessee of the house, and ensure that the appraisal report is delivered to the person whose property is being demolished or the lessee of the house before the ruling is made. If the administrative ruling authority for house demolition makes an administrative ruling on house demolition without ascertaining this issue and cannot provide evidence to prove that the appraisal report of the demolished house has been delivered to the person whose property is being demolished or the lessee of the house, the administrative ruling on house demolition thus made constitutes unclear facts, insufficient main evidence, and violates legal procedures. If the person whose property is being demolished or the lessee of the house files a lawsuit with the People's Court requesting the revocation of such ruling, the People's Court shall support it.

Plaintiff: Lu Tingzuo, male, 69 years old, residing at Lane 658, Nanlin Road, Shanghai.

Defendant: Shanghai Zhabei District Housing and Land Administration Bureau, domiciled at No. 168, Tianmu Middle Road, Shanghai.

Legal Representative: Li Yaping, Director of the Bureau.

Third Party: Shanghai Shenghe Sheng Real Estate Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 380, Tianmu Middle Road, Shanghai.

Legal Representative: Jiang Jie, Chairman of the Company.

Plaintiff Lu Tingzuo, dissatisfied with the house demolition administrative ruling No. (2005) 169 issued by the defendant Shanghai Zhabei District Housing and Land Administration Bureau (hereinafter referred to as Zhabei Housing Bureau), filed an administrative lawsuit with the Zhabei District People's Court of Shanghai.

Plaintiff Lu Tingzuo alleged: The plaintiff's father owned a batch of real estate in plots such as Lane 691, Haining Road, Shanghai. Due to a conflict with the defendant Zhabei Housing Bureau over the ownership of the property, an agreement on house demolition compensation could not be reached. Therefore, the defendant should have recused itself and should not have made a ruling on the dispute over demolition compensation and resettlement between the plaintiff and the third party, Shanghai Shenghe Sheng Real Estate Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shenghe Sheng Company); the "Detailed Implementation Rules of Shanghai Municipality for Urban Housing Demolition and Relocation Management" was not enacted by the Shanghai Municipal People's Congress and cannot serve as the legal basis for the house demolition ruling; the demolishing party, i.e., the third party Shenghe Sheng Company, did not deliver the appraisal report of the demolished house to the plaintiff, and this appraisal report cannot be used as factual evidence for the house demolition ruling. The plaintiff requested the revocation of the house demolition administrative ruling No. (2005) 169 issued by the defendant.

The defendant Zhabei Housing Bureau argued: The defendant has no legal interest in the plaintiff Lu Tingzuo's house, so the defendant has the authority to make a ruling on the dispute over demolition compensation and resettlement between the third party Shenghe Sheng Company and the plaintiff; the defendant determined the area of the demolished house involved based on the property title certificate of the demolished house, and the evidence is sufficient; the appraisal report of the demolished house involved has been delivered to the plaintiff, and this appraisal report can be used as the factual basis for the ruling. The defendant requested the maintenance of the specific administrative act being sued.

The third party Shenghe Sheng Company stated: On December 25, 2003, the third party delivered demolition materials including the appraisal report of the demolished house involved to the plaintiff Lu Tingzuo's home. When signing the receipt, the plaintiff's son, Lu Da, crossed out the appraisal report from the list of delivered materials. The witnesses at the time of delivery, Shen Meizhen and Lu Lihua, staff members of the Changchun Neighborhood Committee, Beizhan Street, Zhabei District, Shanghai, issued a statement explaining that the appraisal report had been delivered to the plaintiff; the structure and floor level of three other houses on the second floor of the same building, occupied by other residents, were superior to those of the demolished house involved, but their appraised unit prices were lower than the average market unit price of existing public housing sold within the same area. Therefore, the appraised unit price confirmed in the appraisal report of the demolished house involved is consistent with the facts. The challenged house demolition ruling is correct, and the third party requested its maintenance.

The Zhabei District People's Court of Shanghai found through trial:

On October 30, 2003, the third party Shenghe Sheng Company obtained the house demolition permit No. (2003) 18 to implement demolition on the plot where Lane 691, Haining Road, Shanghai is located. Plaintiff Lu Tingzuo is the owner of the property at Room ①, First Floor, No. 22, Lane 691, Haining Road, Shanghai, with a building area of 12.48 square meters, plus an attic of 18.37 square meters, totaling 30.85 square meters. After appraisal by Shanghai Real Estate Appraisers Co., Ltd., the appraised unit price was RMB 3,510 per square meter. As no agreement could be reached on the issue of demolition compensation and resettlement, on May 24, 2005, Shenghe Sheng Company submitted an application for a house demolition ruling to the defendant Zhabei Housing Bureau. After accepting the application on the same day, Zhabei Housing Bureau presided over mediation twice on May 26, 2005 and June 15, 2005, respectively, but mediation was not possible because Lu Tingzuo did not attend. Zhabei Housing Bureau then issued the house demolition administrative ruling No. (2005) 169 on June 16, 2005, with the following contents: 1. Lu Tingzuo's household (including users of the house) shall move out of No. 22, Lane 691, Haining Road, Shanghai [Location: Room ①, First Floor (plus an attic)] within 15 days from the date of receipt of the ruling, and move to Room 202, No. 30, Lane 307, Yueluo Road, Shanghai; 2. Lu Tingzuo shall pay Shenghe Sheng Company a one-time difference in price for the area-standard house exchange, in the amount of RMB 130,059.57, upon delivery of the house by Shenghe Sheng Company; 3. Shenghe Sheng Company shall pay Lu Tingzuo fees for relocation of household facilities and other expenses in accordance with the relevant provisions of Document Hu Jia Shang (2002) No. 010.

It was also found that the plaintiff Lu Tingzuo's parents' generation had rented out houses in areas such as Lane 691, Haining Road, Shanghai. In 1958, these rented houses were subjected to socialist transformation in the form of state leasing.

The evidence confirming the above facts includes:

1. House demolition permit No. (2003) 18, and notifications for extension of house demolition period No. (2004) 16 and No. (2004) 36;
2. The household registration of plaintiff Lu Tingzuo and the Shanghai Real Estate Title Certificate for No. 22, Lane 691, Haining Road, Shanghai;
3. The demolition compensation appraisal individual household report (i.e., the appraisal report of the demolished house) issued by Shanghai Real Estate Appraisers Co., Ltd. on December 11, 2003 for the first-floor house at No. 22, Lane 691, Haining Road, Shanghai, and the receipt for delivery dated December 25;
4. Records of conversations between the third party Shenghe Sheng Company and the plaintiff and his family members on September 18, October 13, October 30, November 8, November 26, and December 3, 2004;
5. A return slip for house viewing issued by the third party to the plaintiff's household;
6. The Shanghai Real Estate Title Certificate for Room 202, No. 30, Lane 307, Yueluo Road, Shanghai;
7. The real estate appraisal individual household report (i.e., the appraisal report for the resettlement house) issued by Shanghai Real Estate Appraisers Co., Ltd. on March 14, 2004 for Room 202, No. 30, Lane 307, Yueluo Road, Shanghai;
8. The application for a house demolition ruling submitted by the third party to the defendant Zhabei Housing Bureau on May 24, 2005, the notice of acceptance issued by the defendant, the meeting notice and delivery receipt issued on May 24, the minutes of May 26, the second meeting notice of June 8, three delivery receipts and photos of the posted notice, and the minutes of June 15;
9. The house demolition administrative ruling No. (2005) 169, two delivery receipts, and photos of the posted ruling;
10. A statement issued by Shen Meizhen and Lu Lihua, staff members of the Changchun Neighborhood Committee, Beizhan Street, Zhabei District, Shanghai, stamped by the neighborhood committee;
11. The "Shanghai Urban House Demolition Appraisal Individual Household Reports" for three other houses on the second floor of No. 22, Lane 691, Haining Road, Shanghai, and delivery receipts.

Among the above evidence, evidence 1-10 was provided by the defendant Zhabei Housing Bureau, and evidence 11 was provided by the third party Shenghe Sheng Company.

In view of the plaintiff Lu Tingzuo's objections to the delivery of the appraisal report of the demolished house and to the determination of the location and unit price of the demolished house in the appraisal report, during the first instance, the Zhabei District People's Court of Shanghai explained to the plaintiff: if he had objections to the appraisal result, he had the right to apply for evaluation by the Expert Committee for House Demolition Appraisal during the litigation. The plaintiff explicitly stated that he would not apply for evaluation.

The Zhabei District People's Court of Shanghai held that:

The "Detailed Implementation Rules of Shanghai Municipality for Urban Housing Demolition and Relocation Management" is a regulation promulgated by the Shanghai Municipal People's Government. It does not conflict with higher-level laws and has legal effect. The defendant Zhabei Housing Bureau, as the management department for house demolition work, has the statutory authority to make house demolition rulings within its administrative region. During the demolition process, the demolishing party shall deliver the appraisal report to the owner of the demolished house to protect the owner's right to apply for a re-evaluation of the appraisal report. In this case, the plaintiff Lu Tingzuo alleged that he did not receive the appraisal report of the demolished house involved. The court lawfully granted Lu Tingzuo the right to apply for evaluation by the Expert Committee for House Demolition Appraisal, but Lu Tingzuo stated that he would not apply for evaluation, which constitutes a waiver of that right. The appraisal report of the demolished house involved was made by a qualified appraiser, Shanghai Real Estate Appraisers Co., Ltd. The appraised unit price for the demolished house involved as determined in the report, along with the appraised unit prices for other houses on the same floor with better locations and conditions, were all lower than the average market unit price of existing public housing sold within the same area. The defendant Zhabei Housing Bureau, using the average market unit price of existing public housing sold within the same area as a basis, made a ruling using the method of area-standard house exchange favorable to Lu Tingzuo, which did not infringe on Lu Tingzuo's legitimate rights and interests. After negotiations between the third party Shenghe Sheng Company and Lu Tingzuo during the demolition process resulted in no agreement, Shenghe Sheng Company applied to Zhabei Housing Bureau for a ruling. After accepting Shenghe Sheng Company's application, Zhabei Housing Bureau organized mediation between Lu Tingzuo and Shenghe Sheng Company. Because Lu Tingzuo was absent without cause on two occasions, mediation was impossible. Therefore, within 30 days of accepting Shenghe Sheng Company's application, Zhabei Housing Bureau, based on the basic information of Lu Tingzuo's house at No. 22, Lane 691, Haining Road, Shanghai, the compensation unit price for the demolished house involved, the market price of the resettlement housing, and other factors, and in accordance with the provisions of the "Detailed Implementation Rules of Shanghai Municipality for Urban Housing Demolition and Relocation Management," issued the house demolition administrative ruling No. (2005) 169. This ruling has clear facts, correct application of law, and legal enforcement procedures, and should be upheld.

Accordingly, the Zhabei District People's Court of Shanghai, pursuant to Article 54(1) of the "Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China," rendered a judgment on November 24, 2005:

Upheld the house demolition administrative ruling No. (2005) 169 issued by the defendant Zhabei Housing Bureau on June 16, 2005.

Court acceptance fee of RMB 100 was borne by the plaintiff Lu Tingzuo.

Lu Tingzuo, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Shanghai Second Intermediate People's Court, alleging: The house demolition administrative ruling No. (2005) 169 issued by the appellee Zhabei Housing Bureau on June 16, 2005, erroneously determined the location and area of the appellant's demolished house. According to the "Property Title Transfer List" dated August 14, 1958, submitted by the appellant during the first instance, the demolished house not only included Room ①, First Floor (plus an attic) at No. 22, Lane 691, Haining Road, Shanghai, as determined in the appellee's ruling, but should also include properties such as No. 10 and No. 18, Lane 691, Haining Road, Shanghai; the third party at first instance, Shenghe Sheng Company, never delivered the appraisal report of the demolished house to the appellant, and the appellee failed to ascertain this fact when making the challenged house demolition ruling. The appellant requested the reversal of the original judgment and the revocation of the house demolition administrative ruling No. (2005) 169 issued by Zhabei Housing Bureau on June 16, 2005.

The appellee Zhabei Housing Bureau argued: The third party at first instance, Shenghe Sheng Company, only applied for a ruling on the issue of demolition compensation and resettlement for Room ①, First Floor (plus an attic) at No. 22, Lane 691, Haining Road, Shanghai. Based on the real estate title certificate for that demolished house, the appellee determined the building area of the demolished house to be 30.85 square meters, and there was nothing improper in issuing the house demolition administrative ruling No. (2005) 169 accordingly; based on evidence such as the statement issued by the Changchun Neighborhood Committee, Beizhan Street, Zhabei District, Shanghai on December 25, 2003, provided by Shenghe Sheng Company during the first instance, it can be proven that the appraisal report of the demolished house involved had been delivered to the appellant. Therefore, the appellee requested the dismissal of the appeal and affirmation of the original judgment.

The third party at first instance, Shenghe Sheng Company, agreed with the above defense arguments of the appellee Zhabei Housing Bureau.

During the second instance, the appellee Zhabei Housing Bureau again provided a delivery receipt signed by the appellant Lu Tingzuo's son, Lu Da, on December 25, 2003, which had already been submitted during the first instance, to prove that the appellee had delivered the appraisal report of the demolished house involved to the appellant. In response, the appellant argued that the item "House Appraisal Report" on this delivery receipt had been crossed out from the list of delivered materials, so this evidence cannot prove that the appraisal report of the demolished house involved had been delivered to the appellant.

During the second instance, the third party at first instance, Shenghe Sheng Company, again provided a statement issued by Shen Meizhen and Lu Lihua, staff members of the Changchun Neighborhood Committee, Beizhan Street, Zhabei District, Shanghai, stamped by the neighborhood committee, which had already been submitted during the first instance, to prove that the appraisal report of the demolished house involved had been delivered to the appellant. The main content of this statement was: The appellant Lu Tingzuo's household's appraisal report, relocation promotional materials, and other materials were delivered accompanied by neighborhood committee cadres, and all materials were received by Lu Tingzuo's son, Lu Da, including the appraisal report of the demolished house involved. Upon receiving the materials, Lu Da expressed dissatisfaction with the appraisal report of the demolished house involved. Regarding this evidence, the appellant argued that the "Witness" column on the delivery receipt signed by his son Lu Da was blank, indicating that there was no witness present when the materials were delivered, which contradicts the statement issued by Shen Meizhen and Lu Lihua. Therefore, the appellant did not recognize the evidentiary effect of this statement.

The Shanghai Second Intermediate People's Court found during the second instance:

On the delivery receipt provided by the appellee Zhabei Housing Bureau, signed by the appellant Lu Tingzuo's son Lu Da, the item "House Appraisal Report" had been crossed out from the list of delivered materials, and the delivery receipt did not otherwise note the delivery of the house appraisal report. On this delivery receipt, the "Witness" column was blank, and there was no record of accompaniment by Shen Meizhen and Lu Lihua, staff members of the Changchun Neighborhood Committee, Beizhan Street, Zhabei District, Shanghai, during the delivery. During the process of Zhabei Housing Bureau's issuance of the house demolition administrative ruling No. (2005) 169, Shenghe Sheng Company did not submit the above delivery receipt to Zhabei Housing Bureau.

The above facts are confirmed by evidence such as the house demolition permit No. (2003) 18, the Shanghai Real Estate Title Certificate No. Hu Fang Di Zha Zi (2001) No. 029102, the application for a house demolition ruling, the notice of acceptance, the meeting notice, the investigation records, and the trial records of the first and second instances, which is sufficient to establish.

The Shanghai Second Intermediate People's Court affirmed the first-instance judgment's determination of other facts in this case.

The issues to be resolved in this appeal were: 1. Before the third party at first instance, Shenghe Sheng Company, applied to the appellee Zhabei Housing Bureau for a ruling on the demolished house involved, had the appraisal report of the demolished house involved been delivered to the appellant Lu Tingzuo; 2. If the appraisal report of the demolished house involved had not been delivered to Lu Tingzuo, would this affect the legality of the house demolition administrative ruling No. (2005) 169 issued by Zhabei Housing Bureau.

The Shanghai Second Intermediate People's Court held during the second instance:

On the delivery receipt provided by the appellee Zhabei Housing Bureau, signed by the appellant Lu Tingzuo's son Lu Da, the item "House Appraisal Report" had been crossed out from the list of delivered materials, and the delivery receipt did not otherwise note the delivery of the house appraisal report. Therefore, based on this delivery receipt, it cannot be proven that the house appraisal report had been delivered to the appellant; on this delivery receipt, the "Witness" column was blank, and there was no record of accompaniment by Shen Meizhen and Lu Lihua, staff members of the Changchun Neighborhood Committee, Beizhan Street, Zhabei District, Shanghai, during the delivery. Therefore, it cannot be determined that Shen Meizhen and Lu Lihua were present as witnesses during the delivery of the materials. Consequently, although Shen Meizhen and Lu Lihua issued a statement stamped by the Changchun Neighborhood Committee, Beizhan Street, Zhabei District, Shanghai, and the appellee and the third party at first instance, Shenghe Sheng Company, claimed based on this that they had delivered the house appraisal report to the appellant accompanied by Shen Meizhen and Lu Lihua, this statement contradicts the record on the delivery receipt and also cannot prove that the house appraisal report had been delivered to the appellant. In summary, based on the existing evidence in this case, it cannot be determined that before the third party at first instance applied to the appellee for a ruling on the demolished house involved, the appellant had been delivered the appraisal report of the demolished house involved.

During the demolition process, based on the principle of due process, in order to protect the legitimate rights and interests of the person whose property is being demolished and the lessee of the house, the appraisal report of the demolished house should be delivered to the person whose property is being demolished and the lessee of the house, to ensure that they are promptly informed of the appraisal result for the demolished house, and if they have objections to the appraisal result, they can promptly raise their opinions and apply for a re-evaluation. The demolition ruling authority, during the ruling process, should review the issue of whether the appraisal report of the demolished house has been delivered to the person whose property is being demolished and the lessee of the house. As mentioned above, based on the existing evidence in this case, it cannot be determined that before the third party at first instance, Shenghe Sheng Company, applied to the appellee Zhabei Housing Bureau for a ruling on the demolished house involved, the appraisal report of the demolished house involved had been delivered to the appellant Lu Tingzuo, and the delivery receipt was not submitted to Zhabei Housing Bureau during the ruling process. Zhabei Housing Bureau did not ascertain the fact of whether the appraisal report of the demolished house involved had been delivered to the appellant at all, and then made the house demolition administrative ruling No. (2005) 169 based on the appraisal report. This ruling has insufficient main evidence and violates legal procedures, and should be revoked according to law. The first-instance judgment upholding this ruling was improper and should be corrected.

In summary, the Shanghai Second Intermediate People's Court, pursuant to Article 54(2) and Article 61(3) of the "Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China," rendered a judgment on February 27, 2006:

1. Revoked the first-instance administrative judgment rendered by the Zhabei District People's Court of Shanghai in this case;
2. Revoked the house demolition administrative ruling No. (2005) 169 issued by the appellee Zhabei Housing Bureau on June 16, 2005;
3. Ordered the appellee Zhabei Housing Bureau to make a new house demolition ruling regarding the demolished house involved.

Court acceptance fees of RMB 100 for both the first and second instances were borne by the appellee Zhabei Housing Bureau.

This judgment is final.
